hints: Look closely at each fatty acid tail in X, Y and Z for kinks with double lines. A straight zig-zag means no double bond, a kink with a double line means C=C.
Remember saturated means zero C=C bonds, unsaturated means one or more C=C bonds. Different means compare both chain length and number of double bonds.
walkthrough:
**Spot saturated versus unsaturated tails**

Look for $C=C$ double bonds in the hydrocarbon tails. A straight zig-zag chain has only single bonds, so it is saturated. A chain with one or more double bonds is unsaturated.

X has 1 straight chain plus 2 chains with double bonds. Y has 1 straight chain plus 2 chains with double bonds. Z has 3 straight chains with no double bonds.

**Decide who contains which type**

Because X and Y each have at least one straight chain, plus chains with double bonds, they contain both saturated and unsaturated fatty acids. Z has only straight chains, so it contains only saturated fatty acids.

**Count how many different fatty acids**

In X, all three tails differ in length and in number of double bonds (0, 1 and 3). In Y, all three tails differ (1, 0 and 2 double bonds). In Z, the tails are all saturated and only two lengths are present, so there are not more than two different types.

That gives: saturated in X, Y and Z, unsaturated in X and Y only, more than two different in X and Y only, which is row A.

options.A: Correct. X, Y and Z all have at least one saturated tail, only X and Y have unsaturated tails, and only X and Y have three clearly different tails.
options.B: False. Z has no C=C bonds, so it cannot be listed under contains unsaturated fatty acids.
options.C: False. Z does contain saturated fatty acids, so leaving Z out of the first column is wrong, and Z has no unsaturated tails.
options.D: False. X and Y also contain saturated fatty acids, not just Z, and Z does not have more than two different fatty acids.
